To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystal structure of the SARS‐Co V papain‐like proteinase (PLpro, a cysteine protease) C112S mutant complexed with ubiquitin (a protein modification tag) has been solved at 1.40 Å resolution.

the crystal structure of the Severe acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS‐coronavirus) papain‐like proteinase (PLpro or 3C‐like proteinase) in complex with ubiquitine was determined and the molecular basis of its catalytic mechanism was revealed, and that the structure also provides the molecular basis for the design of novel PLpro inhibitors.
the crystal structure of the SARS‐CoVs PLpro in complex with ubiquitine has been reported, which provides atomic insights into the catalytic process and inhibitor binding of this protease.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the SARS‐Co‐V PLpro–ubiquitin complex structure provides a molecular basis for the catalytic mechanism of PLpro and for its ubiquitin‐like binding mode.
the C terminus of ubiquitin mimics the substrate peptide and is recognized by the SARS-CoV PLpro.
the C‐terminal Leu–Arg‐Gly–Gly of Ub is recognized by PLpro, which provides the first atomic insights of how PLpro recognizes and de‐conjugates Ub from its substrate proteins.
